raw_response:
Well, let me think through this year on my land.

I've got 12.4 mu. About 8 mu I do wheat-maize — that's the usual way, wheat in winter, maize after. The other 4.4 mu I keep in cotton, over by the west plot. That land's a bit saltier, cotton does alright there and the cash from cotton helps even though picking is tiring. My wife and I mostly do the farm work. Two of my sons work in town, one comes back to help at wheat harvest and cotton picking time.

The wheat's already in the ground since last October. Right now it's jointing, so I need to topdress soon. I usually put one bag of urea per mu at planting with the compound, then another half-bag when it turns green in spring, and maybe a bit more at jointing if it looks pale. Same as my neighbor Old Wang does. I'll water it once for returning green, once at jointing, and once more at grain filling if the rain doesn't come. Three times usually.

Maize goes in right after wheat comes off in June — no time to rest the land, maybe five days. I buy hybrid seed at the town store, whatever the shopkeeper recommends that everyone's planting. Put a bag of compound down with the seed, then urea when it's knee-high. One irrigation at tasseling if dry.

Cotton I'm planting now, end of April. Use the seeds from the co-op. Cotton takes more spray than grain — bollworms, aphids — I'll spray maybe four or five times through summer. Fertilizer I don't go too heavy on cotton, it makes the plants too leafy.

Money's tight as always. I'll buy fertilizer in batches when I have cash.
